sentences.text: Drepanaspis was an extinct genus of armoured jawless fish that lived during the Early Devonian period, approximately 416 to 397 million years ago.
This fish possessed a dorsally oriented mouth opening, a distinct feature that separates it from other heterostracan relatives.
Its carapace was broad, depressed, and obtusely rounded at the front, composed of overlapping ventral and dorsal plates or scales.
The carapace features a characteristic V-shaped pattern of tubercles, with approximately 8.5 tubercles per centimeter, which helps identify the specimen's symmetry plane.
Long, elongated, and pointed postero-lateral or cornual plates form most of the exterior margin of the dorsal shield along the posterior end.
The widely spaced eyes, sensory canals, and flattened morphology suggest it was likely a bottom feeder that foraged on the ocean floor.
Members of Drepanaspis possess a complex lateral line sensory system consisting of closed canals within the dermal plates.
Observations of well-developed eyes in associated fossils suggest Drepanaspis lived in shallow offshore waters ranging from 40 to 60 meters in depth.
The first fossils of Drepanaspis were found in 1887 in the Gemünden slate of Rhineland, Germany, and were first described by Clemens August Schlüter.
Scottish palaeoichthyologist Ramsay H. Traquair notably studied the fossils and created the first outline restorations of articulated Drepanaspis specimens.
In 2004, Alain Bleick and his team uncovered more Drepanaspis specimens in the Ardenne Massif of Belgium and Luxembourg, extending the geographical record to the middle-upper Emsian period.
The lateral line sensory system in Drepanaspis likely helped detect changes in water pressure and movement, influencing its behavioral patterns.
The diverse marine fauna found in the Gemünden slate strongly indicates that Drepanaspis was of marine origin.
The genus Drepanaspis was originally described by Schlüter in 1887.
The genus Drepanaspis was originally placed under the authority of Traquair in 1899.
The type species of the genus Drepanaspis is Drepanaspis gemuendenensis.
The genus Drepanaspis includes several species, including D. gemuendenensis, D. sehrieli, D. lipperti, D. jaegeri, D. earteri, and D. edwardsi.
Drepanaspis is classified within the clade Drepanaspididae, which is part of the family Psammosteida.
The family Psammosteida, containing Drepanaspis, belongs to the order Pteraspidiformes and the class Pteraspidomorphi, a major group within the paraphyletic Ostracodermi.
Drepanaspis lived during the Pragian to Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 399.5 million years ago.
The debate over the nature of radial ridges on Drepanaspis plates continued until a specimen from the Odenspiel quarry supported W. Gross's original observation.
There was initial debate regarding whether the dorsal orientation of the Drepanaspis mouth opening was natural or caused by specimen crushing.
